newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Apple Fields updates orchard-to-houses plan.
newsitem.headline: Apple Fields updates orchard-to-houses plan.

text.p: Apple Fields Ltd said on Friday it planned to put detailed strategies for the redevelopment of its orchard properties into housing and private smallholding units before shareholders on May 15.

The plans, launched in December when the company failed in an attempt to become an independent orcharder outside the powerful industry cooperative Apple and Pear Marketing Board (NZAPMB), have made good progress with Canterbury regional councils, the firm said in a statement.
"There is an acceptance (by councils) of the need to meet the expanded demand for sections in order to satisfy present and predicted shortages of land for development," it said.
The proposed developments include large-scale residential villages and what Apple Fields calls "themed quality lifestyle lots", for which marketing strategies are in place.
Proposals involve approval for between 2,000 and 2,500 (housing) sections towards the middle of 1998 with development expected to begin on one of the villages later that year.
"The section sales programme is predicted to continue for between six and 10 years depending on location," it added, saying it discussing possible joint ventures with investors and large developers.
Most of the orchards are currently sub-let to apple growers.
Apple Fields said it did not have any further update on ongoing talks to sell its 52 percent stake in Dairy Brands New Zealand Ltd, a dairy wholesaler and foods supplier.

However, it said parties to placement discussions, under a process already agreed with DBNZ, included local and offshore processors and New Zealand-based companies, "some of whom are not presently industry players".
The group also signalled it had not yet turned its back on its struggle to find a less centralised approach to apple farming.

The statement added that Apple Fields wanted to maintain its present position "alongside the New Zealand apple industry, in order to benefit from the opportunities that it expects to evolve from the gathering momentum for reform".

It said its general strategy remained to evolve into a large residential developer and specialised investor, and it planned to further reduce debt and enter into appropriate joint ventures to strengthen those roles.
